title: Javadoc and API documentation with OpenAPI

videos.script: The bookshop answers HTTP. It sells books, takes orders and hands out tokens. Who knows how to call it? Today, only somebody who reads the source. {{source}} This lesson writes documentation for two different readers. {{readers}} The first works inside the code: a Java developer calling your classes. For them there is Javadoc. Comments with tags, turned into web pages by a tool that comes with the JDK. {{javadoc}} The second reader never sees the code. A front-end developer, a partner's team, a program that generates a client. For them there is OpenAPI: one document describing every path, every parameter and every answer. {{openapi}} You do not write that document by hand. A library called springdoc builds it from the running application. {{springdoc}} Then you read what it built, and some of it is wrong. You fix that with annotations, and declare which calls need a token. {{annotations}} You open Swagger UI, a page that turns the document into forms you can send. {{swagger}} And you decide what a production server should not publish at all. {{production}}
